title: My reaction: an honest review with no words
summary: Show something from your niche on screen, then give your honest opinion with your face alone. AI picks the topics and writes the captions.
why: A Reels trend roundup published October 23, 2026 lists "My reaction" as a new October format: creators pick something from their niche and give an honest opinion using only facial expressions, over original audio.
steps: Use the main prompt to get a list of things in your niche that people have strong feelings about.
Pick one and put it on screen as a short caption, or hold it up to the camera.
Film a few seconds of your face reacting. No talking. Let your expression do the review.
Post it and ask viewers to guess or share their own reaction in the comments.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: My niche is [your niche, for example home cooking, running or houseplants]. I'm making short videos where I show one thing and react with my face only, no words. Write 12 short on-screen captions naming things in my niche that people love, hate or argue about. Mix easy wins, mild debates and a few surprises. Each caption under 8 words. Harmless and fun. No real people, no brands, no politics, no health or money topics, no emojis.

prompts.label: Variation: rate the reaction
prompts.text: For each of these topics: [paste your list], suggest which facial reaction would be funniest (slow smile, confused squint, disappointed stare, pure joy, and so on) and one short caption to add at the end, under 6 words, that tells viewers my final verdict. Keep it light. No emojis.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run [your type of business]. Write 10 short on-screen captions for wordless reaction videos about my work. Include common customer requests, new products, before-and-after results and behind-the-scenes moments. Example for a bakery: "When someone orders the last cinnamon bun." Each under 10 words. Warm and playful, never mocking a real customer. No emojis.

tips: Hold the reaction for two or three seconds. Rushing it kills the joke.
Film in good light, close to the camera, so small expressions show.
Never react to a real person, a real customer's order or a competitor. Keep it about things, not people.
Read the AI's list and cut anything that could hurt someone's feelings.
